Subject: Sudden p99 spike + 500s across several routes

Jordan —

We started seeing a big regression at ~08:50 PST: p99 latency for inference calls to the /v1/chat endpoint jumped from ~340ms to 2.3s, and our error rate climbed to ~6% (mostly 500s). This is happening across our US region and is impacting live traffic for triage flows. Attaching a short request sample and an ops dump.

We’re on the standard hosted plan (account: ClearSky Health). Can you escalate? Our clinical workload is in production and this is user-facing.

Sample symptoms:
- p50 ~450ms, p95 ~900ms, p99 ~2.3s
- 5xx spikes correspond with request bursts from a single prefix (user-session token)
- Our retry logic is now magnifying tail latency

Thanks,

Anna / Jordan — quick update from initial triage (INF-3479):
- We are seeing a set of hot prefixes from ClearSky (same user-session token family) that are dominating a small fraction of the KV cache. The cache eviction rate for that tenant jumped ~12x in the window.
- The runtime’s per-prefix lock for KV cache lookups is causing head-of-line (HOL) lane blocking when a hot key triggers a synchronous fetch (backend miss) and the lane is holding a lock while waiting for KV backend. Concurrent requests behind that lock stall and cause batching lanes to starve; when lanes stall we see increased tail latency and some requests eventually hit error paths.
- TTLs for several per-tenant cache entries are configured very short (10s) on ClearSky’s account; combined with their bursty pattern this produces rapid churn and high eviction churn (cache thrash).

Proposed immediate mitigations (can implement in the next 2–8 hrs):
A) Enable async KV fetch for the affected prefix group (removes per-request lock hold) — low risk, config toggle.
B) Bump TTL for session/prefix entries from 10s -> 120s for ClearSky only — will reduce churn while we investigate working set.
C) Temporarily route ClearSky to a dedicated serving pool (Reserved lane) to isolate from noisy neighbor eviction effects.
D) Apply a hot-key short-circuit: if a single key is >80% of lane occupancy, bypass KV and serve from degraded mode until warmup completes.

I’ve created a short JIRA (INF-3479) with the heap/trace snippets. I’ll provision a canary config and push A/B config to dev first.

Vivek Kulkarni
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference

Attachments: rdw_heapdump_20270209_1002.log (generated), INF-3479-trace.txt
